title: How a Diode Turns AC Into DC Explained Simply | PUC, CBSE and ISC
description:
Aarav plugs in his phone charger. The wall socket gives AC that flips 50 times a second, but the battery needs one-way DC. How does the charger fix that? We start with a water pipe and a one-way flap, then meet the real part: the diode, forward biased and reverse biased.

On a live breadboard an AC supply, one diode and a load run in slow motion while the oscilloscope shows the input (CH1) and the output (CH2): humps in the positive half, zero in the negative half. We derive V_dc = V_m/π (about 0.318 V_m) and I_dc = I_m/π, then the three numbers exams love: peak inverse voltage = V_m, output frequency = input frequency, maximum efficiency 40.6%. A worked example, the exam trap (50 Hz in gives 50 Hz out, not 100 Hz), where it is asked, an original JEE Main pattern practice question with a full solution, and a formula card to screenshot.

This is Episode 42 of PUC Electronics. Karnataka I PUC Electronics Ch 6: Semiconductors, Diodes and Applications of Diodes | NCERT/CBSE Class 12 Physics Ch 14: Semiconductor Electronics: Materials, Devices and Simple Circuits | ISC Class 12 Physics: Semiconductor Electronics (diode as a rectifier).
